A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same survey, with matching title, authors, and core taxonomy. All 22 pages of v1 and 31 pages of v2 were readable, including figures, tables, and references. Neither PDF contains appendices.

before.justification: v1 reviews findings attributed to cited studies and provides illustrative diagrams. It reports no original experiments or quantitative data analysis.

after.justification: Section 4.3 and Table 1 add an original secondary analysis: the authors normalize published agent scores, assign pass/fail classifications, and derive comparative findings. This qualifies as data analysis, although no new gameplay experiments are reported.

M1.justification: The new PBR interaction discussion, hybrid-reasoning illustration, and design guidelines are conceptual recommendations. They do not introduce a specified agent algorithm, architecture, training objective, or implemented procedure.

E1.justification: The added PokerBench and LLM-PySC2 references expand literature coverage, while Table 1 analyzes published performance scores. Neither version reports the authors training or testing agents on datasets or executing additional game scenarios.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates a proposed agent against a baseline set. Table 1 newly compiles agent and human scores from cited studies, but does not establish added or revised comparator experiments.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 introduces a secondary assessment protocol using Relative Agent Score, calculated as agent score divided by perfect score, and a 60% passing threshold. This adds an applied scoring rule without changing the underlying studies' experimental settings.

E4.justification: No empirical ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity analyses, or observed case studies are added. The new game and PBR examples are illustrations; Section 4.3 presents aggregate performance comparisons rather than supplementary diagnostic experiments.

E5.justification: The new performance table reports point scores without repeated-run information, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Neither version establishes an original uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds a substantial numerical performance synthesis absent from v1, including Guandan's 2.17/4 = 54.25% relative score, Prisoner's Dilemma's 34.60%, and Werewolf's 52% agent and human scores. Section 4.3 adds cross-game and human-comparison findings. These are newly reported secondary results, not demonstrated performance gains between versions.

T1.justification: Section 4.3 and Table 1 introduce the mathematical definition of Relative Agent Score and its threshold-based classification. No theorems, proofs, or substantive formal derivations are added; the PBR framework remains conceptual.

C1.justification: The abstract adds module interactions and cross-game performance assessment to the survey's scope. The introduction newly claims a unified, comprehensive performance comparison and detailed development guidelines as core contributions, substantially extending v1's taxonomy-centered contribution.

C2.justification: Section 3.4 adds six directional interpretations of preference, belief, and reasoning interactions. Sections 4.3–6 add performance interpretations, practical tradeoffs, and more concrete research directions. The new Broader Impact Statement discusses deployment risks and explicitly limits generalizability because surveyed studies predominantly use GPT models.

D1.justification: Table 1 newly documents each compiled result's source, backbone model, metric, and score denominator, supporting reconstruction of the normalized scores. Section 2.1 also documents PokerBench's 11,000 scenarios and pre-flop/post-flop breakdown. These are added disclosures, not evidence of changed experimental implementations.

R1.justification: The literature expands to PokerBench, LLM-PySC2, human-persona and demographic studies, Agent-Pro, and QuBE. The revised future directions establish additional connections to multi-agent reinforcement learning, credit assignment, causal analysis, and behavior-pattern mining. The central distinction from earlier surveys remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 expands the introduction's roadmap and contribution statement, adds dedicated interaction, performance-assessment, and practical-guidance sections, and substantially rewrites all four future-direction subsections. It also adds broader-impact and acknowledgment sections, alongside smaller terminology and wording corrections.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 4 explaining game types, Figure 9 illustrating PBR interactions, and two substantive tables. v1's Figure 7 becomes Figure 8 with an additional hybrid-reasoning panel. Most earlier illustrations are retained and renumbered, with smaller diagram-label and citation updates.

improvement.justification: The interaction explanations, practical guidance, and more concrete future directions substantially improve the survey's usefulness. However, the new headline performance assessment compares heterogeneous metrics and backbones without establishing cross-game comparability or calibrating its common passing threshold. Table 1 also marks StarCraft II's 60% as passing despite requiring scores above 60%. These explanatory gains coexist with new weaknesses in a central contribution, leaving the net quality change uncertain.
